comment: The Master Security/Quality Gate (tests/security/master-security-gate.sh) as an inventory of what a Release is asked to run: docs/23_SECURITY_PRIVACY.md §11 (dependency audit, SAST, secret scan, container scan, OWASP smoke, permission E2E) plus the SBOM that docs/25_CICD_DEVOPS.md items 9-10 ask for. Every one of them is listed in `items`, either as covered by named rows of the gate or as an absence. Read and enforced by tests/security/check-absent-manifest.py — the `absence_witness` commands of the remaining absence are RUN by that checker and must still come back empty, so this file cannot go stale quietly. WHAT CHANGED IN v2 (T1209): SAST and the SBOM stopped being absences — they are eight new rows of the gate (sast-go/python/node, sbom-go/node/python, license-audit, container-scan), and the two detail entries that described them are gone rather than left behind as prose about a gap that no longer exists. The container scan stays an absence, because there is still no image to scan; what it gained is a GUARD: a row of the gate that is green only while the tree really has no container build file, that prints why, and that fails the moment one appears. Whether an absent capability is an ACCEPTED V1 RISK is the Supervisor's written call (docs/23 §11 allows a written ADR/risk acceptance for High; Critical is not accepted in V1) — `suggested_disposition` below is the Worker's recommendation, not that call.

kinds.covered: a check of the master gate runs this today; check_ids name it and the checker proves those ids still exist in the gate's registry
kinds.guarded-absence: nothing in this tree performs it, and a named row of the master gate exists whose only job is to keep that visible: the row is green while the absence is real, prints what the absence rests on, and goes red the moment it stops being true. A guard is not the capability — it is a statement about the capability that is allowed to fail.

required_by: docs/23_SECURITY_PRIVACY.md §11 (每个 Release 运行 dependency audit、SAST、secret scan、container scan、OWASP smoke、permission E2E) + docs/25_CICD_DEVOPS.md items 9-10 (security/dependency/secret scan、container build/SBOM)

items.note: Three ecosystems, three instruments, three separate rows: govulncheck (Go, v1.8.0), pnpm audit --audit-level=low (Node/web), uv audit (Python adapter). Each row is red on its own and each one is NOT ASKED — never silently green — on a host that lacks its tool.

Three languages, three instruments, three separate rows, so a red Go scan cannot hide behind a green Node one (tests/security/sast.sh). gosec v2.29.0 reads the Go module, bandit 1.8.6 the adapter's source, eslint 9.39.5 + eslint-plugin-security 4.0.1 + typescript-eslint 8.70.1 the web app and the shared UI package. Every row checks its tool's version against ops/security/tool-versions.sh before scanning, refuses a scan that covered too little of the tree, and requires each finding to be a per-finding baseline entry with a written review — no -exclude-dir, no -nosec, no severity floor anywhere in the invocations. The existing findings are baselined per finding in ops/ci/gosec-baseline.txt, ops/ci/eslint-security-baseline.txt and ops/ci/bandit-baseline.txt; a baseline entry is not an accepted risk (that is a written ADR) and sast_report.py rejects an entry that names a directory, a glob or a rule without a file and line.

internal/config.ScanRepoExampleFiles over every committed *.env.example in the tree, with the detector's own planted-secret failing mode (TestScanRepoExampleFilesFailsOnPlantedFile) required as evidence in the same row: a scanner that stopped scanning goes red here.

tests/security/owasp-smoke.sh against the real API binary, real PostgreSQL and real Redis: the header set value for value, CORS refusals, an anonymous write as 401, the credential rate-limit boundary and the fail-closed path. It is also the G3 job `security-smoke` in specs/orchestrator/gates.json.
tests/e2e/privacy_e2e_test.go — TestE2EPrivacyNegative: the negative path is the point, so the row requires that test to have passed by name.

Still an absence — there is no image in this tree to scan — but no longer an unguarded one: the `container-scan` row of the gate is green only while that is true, and its failure message says what has to replace it. See the entry below.

One document per face, generated and validated by the row that reports it — cyclonedx-gomod v1.9.0 over go.mod, `pnpm sbom` (pnpm pinned by package.json's packageManager) over the installed workspace, `uv export --format cyclonedx1.5` plus the adapter's own dist-info METADATA for licences. A green row means the document was re-parsed, cleared a per-face component floor, and resolved every key component named in tests/security/key-components.json — including the entries whose answer is "not in this tree" and the witness that has to keep saying so. The documents are written to the ignored .sbom/ directory and are never committed: they are reproducible from go.mod, pnpm-lock.yaml and uv.lock, and a committed SBOM is an inventory of a tree that no longer exists. `license-audit` is the row that reads all three (docs/40:3) and judges every component's licence against ops/security/license-allowlist.json, with a written reason per allowed licence and a deny-class that goes red naming package, licence and version.

absent.capability: Scanning built container images for OS-package and application-layer CVEs before they are deployed.

absence_witness.why: the tree has no container build file, so no application image exists to scan — the same walk the guard row performs, run here by the checker itself
the tree claim the guard rests on is still registered, exactly once, in the file the release runbook reads

absent.why_absent: Nothing in this tree builds or runs an application image: there is no Dockerfile anywhere (ops/deploy/README.md § What is missing #1; ops/runbook-steps.json, tree claim `no-dockerfile`, re-derived by ops/runbook-verify.py T1). A container scanner has no artifact to scan, so this is not a tool that is missing — it is the build that is missing. The only images in play are the infrastructure ones pulled by docker-compose.yml (pgvector/pgvector:0.8.6-pg16, redis:7.4.11-alpine, quay.io/minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z, gitea/gitea:1.27.3, axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1), pinned by tag and never scanned by anything here — their licences are now recorded per image in tests/security/key-components.json and judged by the license-audit row, which is a statement about their licence and not about their contents.
absent.guard: The `container-scan` row of the gate (tests/security/container-scan.sh) is this absence made falsifiable. It walks the tree for Dockerfile, Dockerfile.*, *.Dockerfile, Containerfile and Containerfile.*, prints how many files it walked and which claim says there is no image, and exits 0 only while it finds none. It exits 1 the moment one appears — not because the repository broke, but because this row stopped being the truth and a real image scan has to take its place — and it also exits 1 if the `no-dockerfile` claim disappears from ops/runbook-steps.json, since a guard citing a claim nobody registers is a guard resting on nothing. A guarded absence is falsifiable in the direction that matters: it can go red on its own, and it prints why it is green while it is.
absent.substitute_today: The staging template is validated statically and fail-closed: tests/acceptance/deploy-staging-smoke.sh runs 19 rules over ops/deploy/docker-compose.staging.yml, ops/deploy/staging.env.example and the nginx config, including rule R03, which refuses an image pinned by anything other than @sha256:<64 hex>. That is a rule about how an image must be referenced, not a statement about what is inside it. The dependency audits cover the application's own packages, not a base image's OS packages.
absent.to_add: First the image: a Dockerfile per application (api, web, scientific-adapter) plus a build stage in CI (docs/25 item 10). Then the scanner: trivy or grype in image mode over each built image, failing on High/Critical, with an ignore file for accepted findings; and digest pinning for every image the deployment composes, which rule R03 already demands. The guard row must be REPLACED by that scanner, not deleted alongside it: it is the only thing in the tree that says which of the two states the repository is in. The scanner is a day of work once the images exist; the images are the actual project.
absent.impact: Today no deployed artifact exists, so the exposure is the infrastructure stack's upstream images and their update cadence — nobody in this repository tracks them, and a base-image CVE would be found by reading release notes, not by a gate. Once images are built, without this row a High in a base layer ships unnoticed. The guard changes when this becomes visible (immediately, on the commit that adds the Dockerfile) and does not change the exposure itself: nothing is being scanned today either way.
absent.suggested_disposition: Recommend accepting for V1 with the gap stated plainly (there is no image to scan yet), and making the image build + trivy a single follow-up item so that the scanner cannot be split from the artifact that makes it meaningful. The guard is what keeps that acceptance honest: it is a written record that can go red, rather than a paragraph promising someone will notice. Nothing to scan is a reason to defer the scanner; it is not a reason to call the release container-safe.
